tasks.title: VTX power and range
tasks.solution: Received power falls as 1/d², so range ∝ √P: every +3 dB (×2 power) gives ×1.41 range.

tasks.title: Intermodulation of two transmitters
tasks.solution: The third-order products 2f₁ − f₂ and 2f₂ − f₁ sit one pair-spacing away from the pair. If such a product lands on a third pilot's channel (on an even grid, exactly the neighboring one), that pilot gets stripes and snow even though all the frequencies are "different". Outside the 5.8 GHz band it is harmless.

tasks.title: Power level: dBm to mW
tasks.solution: mW = 10^(dBm/10): 0 dBm = 1 mW, every +10 dBm is ×10, every +3 dBm is roughly ×2. That is why 14, 20 and 26 dBm are labeled 25, 100 and 400 mW in powerlabels.

tasks.title: Raceband channel frequency
tasks.solution: Raceband starts at R1 = 5658 MHz and goes in 37 MHz steps: Rn = 5658 + 37 · (n − 1), R8 = 5917. Every other channel (R1, R3, R5, R7) is 74 MHz apart.
